title: What can you say about chromium in your ads and on your site?
summary: The library supports 2 wordings for chromium; the strongest is "Helps maintain normal blood glucose levels" (strong, 6-500 µg a day). Avoid wording that names or implies a disease, a drug or a treatment, such as "Lowers blood sugar, or helps manage diabetes", and keep "Helps maintain normal blood glucose levels" off Meta ads.

supported_wordings.wording: Helps maintain normal blood glucose levels.
supported_wordings.why: Listed by Health Canada and authorized in the EU after EFSA review.
supported_wordings.dose_details: Adults 19 and older. Health Canada: 2.2-500 µg a day. EU: at least 6 µg, 15% of the 40 µg EU reference value (Regulation (EU) No 1169/2011, Annex XIII). ODS: no upper limit was set.
supported_wordings.form: Trivalent chromium from a salt on Health Canada's list (such as picolinate or chloride), counted as chromium

sources.name: Commission Regulation (EU) No 432/2012, list of permitted health claims

supported_wordings.meta_ads: Wording to avoid in Meta ads. On your site it is supported wording.

supported_wordings.why: Authorized in the EU after EFSA review; Health Canada does not list it.
supported_wordings.dose_details: EU: at least 6 µg, 15% of the 40 µg EU reference value (Regulation (EU) No 1169/2011, Annex XIII). Health Canada does not list this wording on its own; its monograph gives chromium at 2.2-500 µg a day for adults.
supported_wordings.form: Trivalent chromium from a salt on Health Canada's list (such as picolinate or chloride), counted as chromium

sources.name: Commission Regulation (EU) No 432/2012, list of permitted health claims

wordings_to_avoid.wording: Lowers blood sugar, or helps manage diabetes
wordings_to_avoid.why: Names a disease. Maintaining normal blood glucose is structure-and-function wording; lowering blood sugar or managing diabetes is not.
Names medical conditions. FDA's only qualified claim here is for chromium picolinate, with set wording (see fda_health_claims).

wordings_to_avoid.wording: Helps maintain normal blood glucose levels.
wordings_to_avoid.why: Blood sugar is a health-condition claim on Meta, so this wording stays off Meta ads, as potassium's blood pressure wording does (library decision of 2026-10-15; Meta's ad policies were not read). It stays supported wording for pages.

evidence_strengths.strong: At least two listed sources support it independently at a comparable dose and form, and none disagrees.
evidence_strengths.moderate: One listed source supports it as an evidence-based use at that dose, and no listed source disagrees.
evidence_strengths.limited: The only support is traditional use, the sources disagree, or the source itself calls the evidence weak.

reasons_to_avoid.drug: names a drug or presents the product as one
reasons_to_avoid.treatment: promises to treat, cure or prevent a condition

disclaimer: Not legal advice. This guide shows the wording that published evidence supports at a daily dose, from the sources linked below; it is not a ruling on any claim. Your own product, its form and dose, and your own evidence still need to match the wording you use.
